newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Spain's Aznar lauds Mercosur trade bloc.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar lauds Mercosur trade bloc.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Friday said South America's Mercosur trade bloc was of the greatest importance to the European Union and to Madrid.

On a three-day visit to Brazil to be followed by a stop-off in neighboring Argentina, two of the four Mercosur members, Aznar said he not just supported but had initiated calls for an EU-Latin American and Caribbean summit, best left till 1999.

"Spain is interested in Mercosur. The European Union is very interested in Mercosur," the Spanish leader told reporters after meeting Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in Brazil's capital Brasilia.
"The only global accord that the EU has is with Mercosur. There is no choice but to bet on Mercosur," Aznar added.

The EU signed a landmark pact in December 1995 setting the stage for eventual free trade talks with the South American customs union, which also includes Uruguay and Paraguay and has associate agreements with Chile and Bolivia.

In a recent visit to the region, French President Jacques Chirac urged Latin America to look less toward the United States and more across the Atlantic. Chirac proposed a summit of EU-Latin American leaders in 1998.

Chirac's suggestion, greeted especially in Brazil, mildly irritated Spanish officials. Aznar had proposed exactly the same thing at a conference in Santiago, Chile, shortly before, without triggering much of a response.
Spain's close cultural ties with Spanish-speaking Latin America have not been matched in Portuguese-speaking Brazil.

Aznar said his visit to Latin America's largest country was aimed not just at boosting trade ties but also political relations and that both he and Cardoso had agreed on the need for a permanent "mechanism" for bilateral consultations.
"We agree that the quality of relations between Spain and Brazil have improved but we want to intensify the political dialogue," he said.

In Brazil's economic powerhouse Sao Paulo on Thursday, the Spanish prime minister told businessmen that Madrid, backed by its historical ties to the region, was determined to act as a bridge between Europe and Latin America.
Last year, Spanish direct investment in Brazil reached $600 million and bilateral trade was nearly $2.0 billion, with Brazil enjoying a rare surplus with a trading partner.

Over lunch, Cardoso and Aznar discussed how investment and trade could be improved and how Brazil, rapidly emerging on the world stage after a period of self-imposed isolation, could play a greater role in international forums, officials said.
Aznar was due to travel on Saturday to the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, where Spain's Telefonica de Espana recently bought a slice of the state-owned telecommunications firm CRT.
After Brazil, he was due to travel to Buenos Aires.
